title: Image Viewer Online – Open HEIC, WebP & TIFF, No Upload
description: Open any picture in your browser: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, TIFF and SVG, with zoom and the photo's camera, date and GPS details. Free, nothing uploaded.
heading: Image Viewer: Open Any Picture Online
subtitle: Drop a picture to zoom in and see the details it carries; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Open a picture online, including formats your computer may not open: iPhone HEIC photos, WebP, AVIF, TIFF and SVG. Zoom in, fit it to the window and see transparent parts on a checkerboard. The details panel lists the camera, lens, date taken and, when the photo carries it, the GPS location, with a link to clean it out.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your pictures are read and changed by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees them.

features.title: See what a photo reveals
features.text: Camera, lens, date taken and GPS location, read from the file's own metadata.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, the tool keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: open a picture online

steps.title: Drop your picture
steps.text: Choose or drop a JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, HEIC, TIFF or SVG file.

steps.title: Look around
steps.text: Zoom in and out, fit the picture to the window, and open the details panel.

steps.title: Take the next step
steps.text: Compress it, resize it, remove its metadata or turn it into a PDF without choosing the file again.

handles: Formats: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF (first frame), BMP, HEIC and HEIF, TIFF (first page) and SVG.
View: zoom from 10% to 800%, fit to the window, and a checkerboard behind transparent parts.
Details: size in pixels, file size, camera, lens, date taken, software and author.
Location: the GPS position a photo carries, with a link to open it on OpenStreetMap when you choose to.
limits: GIF animations show their first frame, and multi-page TIFF files their first page.
A few HEIC photos taken with the newest iPhone settings may not decode; save those as JPG on the phone first.
Very large pictures (above about 100 megapixels) are limited by your device's memory.

faq.question: Are my pictures uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your pictures are read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and are never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: How do I open a HEIC photo on Windows?
faq.answer: Windows opens HEIC photos in its Photos app once the HEIF Image Extensions from the Microsoft Store are installed. Without them, open the photo in OpenAnyDoc's image viewer: Chrome, Edge and Firefox can't show HEIC themselves, so a HEIC decoder loads the first time you open one, and the photo is still read on your device.

faq.question: Why does it say my photo contains my location?
faq.answer: Phones save the GPS position in each photo unless location is turned off for the camera. Anyone you send the original file to can read it.

faq.question: Can I edit the picture here?
faq.answer: The viewer only shows it. Use the next steps above the picture to compress, resize, crop or clean it; the file moves over without being chosen again.

faq.question: Why does an animated GIF not move?
faq.answer: The viewer shows the first frame of an animation. Your browser can still play the GIF itself.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.

faq.question: How do I open a HEIC photo on a Mac or an Android phone?
faq.answer: A Mac opens HEIC photos in Photos and Preview with nothing to install, and most Android phones open them in Google Photos or the phone's own gallery app. When an app or website still refuses one, open it in OpenAnyDoc's image viewer in any browser, or turn it into a JPG with the HEIC to JPG converter.

faq.question: What program opens a .webp file?
faq.answer: Every current web browser opens .webp pictures: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, and so do Photos on Windows and Preview on a Mac. OpenAnyDoc's image viewer shows a WebP file with zoom and its details, and the next steps can turn it into a JPG or PNG without uploading it.
